Based on the idea of a closed-loop or circular economy, we have been systematically conducting life cycle assessments (LCAs) for major product groups since 2017. This entails an evaluation of product-specific environmental aspects in each phase of the life cycle – from purchasing to production and use right through to disposal. Among the evaluated aspects are, for example, the use of materials, the consumption of energy and resources in the manufacturing and use phase, recycling and the use of recycled materials, and remanufacturing at the end of the product’s life cycle.

Depending on the use case, we distinguish between two assessment methods: the full- scale LCA, performed in compliance with ISO 14040 and 14044, and the streamlined LCA, allowing faster assessment of specific issues and drawing on standard database values.

New or changing regulatory requirements worldwide – such as CO2-related taxes – may require adjustments to products and technologies and therefore lead to higher costs. Extreme weather events can disrupt processes along the value chain and lead to production and delivery stoppages, breaches of contract or loss of sales. Improper use of such substances and materials in upstream production processes further down the supply chain and improper product disposal can lead to the release of SoCs/SVHCs and thus to environmental pollution.
